result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

args.text: When a described process has different paths that converge before a later activity, model an explicit merge gateway before that activity rather than connecting each incoming path directly to it. This includes a normal path and a path that repeats after an earlier activity.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Build a connected path from each modeled start to an end or intentionally continuing state. Avoid accidental disconnected flow nodes.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.

result.rule: When the description says an activity may take place before a later activity: Model the optional activity as a decision branch with a path that bypasses it; merge the paths before the later activity.

When the description states that an ongoing activity continues while a separate review or decision proceeds: model the activities as concurrent paths with a parallel gateway, and synchronize them before any later step that depends on both paths being complete

When the description states that named activities may be performed as optional additions to the main sequence: Model each named activity in the optional flow, using gateways to reflect whether the activities are alternatives or whether one or more may occur.

When the description states that an implementation can take one of several alternative forms: Model each form as a separate activity on mutually exclusive branches, then merge the branches before the next common activity.

result.rule: When the description says an activity may take place before a later activity: Model the optional activity as a decision branch with a path that bypasses it; merge the paths before the later activity.

When the description states that an ongoing activity continues while a separate review or decision proceeds: model the activities as concurrent paths with a parallel gateway, and synchronize them before any later step that depends on both paths being complete

When the description states that named activities may be performed as optional additions to the main sequence: Model each named activity in the optional flow, using gateways to reflect whether the activities are alternatives or whether one or more may occur.

When the description says a later activity occurs after an earlier activity succeeds but does not describe an alternative outcome or failure handling: Model the stated sequence with a direct sequence flow; do not add a decision gateway solely to represent an unspecified failure path.
